title: verify() accepts message with all-failed signers if at least one succeeds even if that signer's cert is untrusted
description: verify() returns Ok(VerificationResult) when at least one SignerResult.verified == true. verify_one() sets verified=true only after ALL five steps pass including validate_chain(). This is correct. However: a SignedData with N signers where signer 0 has a valid chain but signer 1 is a completely different, malicious entity will still return Ok. The VerificationResult.signers vec exposes all results, so callers who check is_verified() without examining the signers vec may not notice that other signers were rejected. This is not a bug in the logic but the API makes it easy for callers to call is_verified() and miss partial failures. Flag as correctness because is_verified() returns true even if 99 of 100 signers are malicious.
close_reason: Documented behavior: Ok(VerificationResult) means at least one signer verified. Per-signer detail is in the signers vec. Callers who need all-signers-pass can check themselves. Opinion.
